steps.text: Whisk together oil, vinegar, lemon pepper, sugar, and lemon juice. Use a funnel to pour into a clean bottle with a tight fitting lid. Shake bottle before using and pour over favorite green salad.

raw_recipe.headline: Magical Dressing
raw_recipe.description: We're going to tell you the secret for this very good dressing. It's the brown sugar and lemon pepper. They perform alchemy with the other three ingredients: olive oil, balsamic vinegar, and lemon juice. Makes one cup.
raw_recipe.name: Magical Dressing

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk together oil, vinegar, lemon pepper, sugar, and lemon juice. Use a funnel to pour into a clean bottle with a tight fitting lid. Shake bottle before using and pour over favorite green salad.

review.reviewBody:
Good dressing, but I can't say it was outstanding.
Needs garlic, oregano, etc. for a little more flavor or zip.

This dressing was very good. Here's a variation I used. Simmer some balsamic vinegar until it is reduces (the more it simmers, the sweeter it will be). You may want to play with the ratios of olive oil/vinegar until you get it to your liking. And you can then cut back (or eliminate) the brown sugar. I made this with adding an avocado (mash up half of it, leave the the other half in chunks). It gives a sweet and nutty dressing. Don't omit a squirt of lemon juice. You definitely need the acid to help balance the sweet.
For a French (Catalina-like) twist swap out the sugar for 2 T ketchup. Really good! Also helps the emulsion hold together.

This would be more magical if the recipe included salt and had a different ratio of vinegar to oil -- I like a little less vinegar in my vinaigrettes. I made this as directed other than adding salt after I realized there was none included. With salt this is 5 stars, without it, 4 stars because it is a little flat. Thanks for sharing!

I've pretty much stopped buying salad dressing, because I use this recipe exclusively. I leave out the lemon pepper- there's already lemon juice- and I throw in a pinch of red pepper flakes for a small zip. I've also tried it with a hint of garlic, but either way, the olive oil, balsamic vinegar, brown sugar, and lemon juice are all you need for the best dressing. Thanks for sharing, Laura!
Simple and good. What's not to like? That said, I make mine with chopped garlic and to sweeten it a bit, maple syrup. I also tend use a ratio of 3:1 oil to vinegar.
Thiß is yummy ,..I love a salad and this dressing is ideal..,it tastes really nice ,the touch of lemon pepper makes a huge difference..,.I left the garlic out because I simply do not like it..,

I think this was a delicious recipe, but I admit to one change out of necessity! As I reached for my Olive Oil, I remembered I had forgotten to pick up a new bottle! I had perhaps 1 T. left! Not wanting to run out to the grocers, I recalled a gift I had received from a dear friend. I had been waiting for a 'special' recipe to dip into a bottle of Sicilian Orange infused Olive Oil. Well, this was it! I subbed in half SOOO, 1 T. leftover 'regular' OO, and the balance of the second half Canola Oil! The result was/is delicious! The beautiful citrus combination of the lemon juice and the orange infusion in the subbed Olive Oil, worked so perfectly! All in all, what started as a great base recipe, was by happenstance, a fabulous variant! A sprinkle of kosher salt and a few grinds of black pepper as each person desired, and it was complete! This dressing was indeed 'Magical'! Thank you!

I am truly impressed with this dressing! I added a touch of extra brown sugar to enhance its flavor, which perfectly balanced out the slight bitterness I encountered earlier. It made a remarkable difference!
So delicious! I served it on spring mix with dried cranberries and spiced pecans and everyone enjoyed it. Thanks for submitting this recipe!

An uncomplicated and quick to make salad dressing that has very good flavor despite having so few ingredients. I used good quality balsamic vinegar so I only needed 2/3 of the requested amount of brown sugar.

If you're a "I only cook chicken breasts because they are canvas for other flavors," or "I need something to kill the taste of lettuce or this salad," or "I'm not really into savory and/or I need something sweet to kill this savory." This is the bomb for you!!! This is your dream come true
I've made this repeatedly and absolutely love it...no additives, no chemicals, especially when using high quality cold-pressed olive oil and organic balsamic vinegar; no more store-bought for me!!
I made a half recipe, just to try it out. We liked it so much that it's now one of our favorites. And it's very easy to make and store.
Very tasty and easy to throw together!
Easy and typically I have all the ingredients in the house, except lemon pepper. Used half lemon white bals vinegar and half white bals vinegar. Used dashes pepper
